specification.problem: Discrete-time coin quantum walk on a cycle of N=2^n sites. An unknown qubit a|0>+b|1> starts as the coin state with the walker at site 0. After t steps, a fixed state-independent single-qubit correction D on the coin should leave the walker at site d with coin state a|0>+b|1>. The task is to test for which (coin, t, d) this succeeds, and to check periodicity of the walk.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Small circle with n=3 (N=8, 4 qubits total). Coins are identity, X, Hadamard and Ry(theta). The statevector gives the transfer fidelity at a fixed site d for the basis inputs |0>, |1>, |+>, |+i> (which fixes the map on the coin by linearity), and the minimal T with U^T=I is found on that subspace. Outside scope: the paper's line-walk theorems, proofs of 'arbitrary distance' versus 'finite distance', the exact definition of D for biased coins, and the exact arbitrary-distance construction for the line.

symbols.meaning: number of sites on the cycle
single-qubit walk coin (I, X, H or Ry(theta))
final correction coin on the coin qubit, independent of a,b
increment/decrement shift on the position register
number of walk steps and target site

equations.label: Shift operator
equations.description: Coin-conditioned shift on the cycle, with coin 0 moving right and coin 1 left. Implemented with controlled increment/decrement circuits.
equations.justification: Convention taken from the method sketch; the abstract names only a walk on a line or circle.
assumptions: Power-of-two cycle so the shift is a modular adder

equations.label: Walk step and transfer state
equations.description: Coin is applied first, then the shift. After t steps D is applied to the coin qubit only.
equations.abstract_quote: we introduce an additional coin operator which is applied at the end of the walk. This operator does not depend on the state to be transferred.
equations.justification: The abstract states a final state-independent coin operator; the step ordering is an assumption.

equations.label: Perfect transfer criterion
equations.description: Success is checked on four inputs; by linearity, fidelity 1 on all four (with consistent phases) gives transfer for every a,b. Checking the two basis states alone would miss relative-phase errors. Read from the statevector with no measurement.
equations.abstract_quote: perfect transfer of an unknown qubit state via the discrete-time quantum walk on a line or a circle
equations.justification: Perfect transfer means the output equals the input state at the target site for all inputs.

equations.label: Identity coin on the circle
equations.latex: U^t|0\rangle(a|0\rangle+b|1\rangle)=a|t\bmod N\rangle|0\rangle+b|-t\bmod N\rangle|1\rangle;\ \text{components meet iff } 2t\equiv0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ N),\ \text{e.g. } t=N/2,\ d=N/2,\ D=I
equations.description: With C=I the two coin components move in opposite directions and coincide on a cycle only at t=N/2, giving transfer to site N/2 with D=I. On an infinite line they never coincide, so the paper's 'any distance' result for this coin must rely on a different definition than the one here.
equations.justification: Direct computation from eq_1 with C=I; related to the abstract only through its identity-coin claim.

equations.label: Flip coin
equations.description: Computed under the coin-then-shift order. For even t the walker is back at site 0 with the original state (D=I), i.e. trivial transfer at distance 0. For odd t the components sit at sites ±1 and are separated, so D cannot merge them. A different shift or coin ordering may give nonzero distances.
equations.justification: Direct computation from eq_1 and eq_2 with C=X; this contradicts the sketch's claim of arbitrary-distance transfer under these conventions.

equations.label: Periodicity
equations.description: Check numerically for each coin that a minimal T exists on the reachable subspace, for example N or 2N for I and X on the cycle. Compare the states for several ψ, including phases.
equations.abstract_quote: we show that quantum walks ending with a perfect state transfer are periodic
equations.justification: The abstract claims periodicity of walks that end in perfect transfer; the exact form of the check is chosen here.
assumptions: Periodicity tested on the subspace reached from |0>⊗coin

registers.name: pos
registers.role: walker position, little-endian integer x=sum x_i 2^i, qubits 0..n-1

registers.name: coin
registers.role: coin qubit (index n) carrying the unknown state, supplied as input by the runner

specification.initial_state: |0>_pos ⊗ (a|0>+b|1>)_coin; the unknown state is supplied by the runner, with no initialize

steps.description: Take the coin qubit in state ψ and the position register in |0>.
Repeat t times: apply coin C (I, X, H or Ry(theta)) on the coin qubit, then the coin-controlled modular increment/decrement S built from cx/ccx/mcx.
Apply the fixed correction D on the coin qubit (D=I for the identity and flip coins; for H/Ry choose D as the inverse of the coin-block unitary found by simulation).
Scan (t,d) from the statevector for fidelity 1. Check against the identity-coin circle prediction t=N/2, d=N/2, and find the minimal period T.

specification.measurement: None. Read the final statevector for the fidelity; the circuit contains no measurement gates.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Project the position onto |d>, compute the reduced coin fidelity with ψ for the four test inputs, and report the minimal period T.
assumptions: Walker starts at site 0 with the unknown qubit as the coin state
Target d is fixed and known
D is a single-qubit unitary on the coin only
Instance n=3 (4 qubits), cyclic shift mod 8
Coin-then-shift ordering and coin-0=right convention are assumed, not from the abstract
missing_information: Exact coin and shift ordering used in the paper
Explicit D for Hadamard and biased coins
Paper's definition of 'distance' on the line and its target-site convention
The construction that makes identity and flip coins work at arbitrary distance on a line
